nodes.title: Electron v39 Fails to Render Styled UI on Fedora/Gnome (Renderer Process Failure)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

last known working version could not be determined because the application failed on every tested version.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

The application is expected to launch, initialize the Chromium renderer process successfully, and display the fully styled Graphical User Interface (GUI) as designed.

The main Electron window should open and present the complete application UI, which includes the styled form fields, and correctly colored buttons (green for Save, indigo for Preview).

The application should not display a blank white screen or an unstyled, bare HTML interface.

The application's internal JavaScript logic (for generating the manifest object) and the secure IPC bridge (window.fileAPI) should initialize without error.

### Actual Behavior

When the application is launched, the following happens:

1.  The main Electron window opens successfully.
2.  The application **fails to render any styling or layout** from the fully embedded CSS.
3.  The user interface is displayed as **plain, unstyled HTML text** (white background, default black font, unstyled buttons).
4.  There is **no crash log or error message** generated; the Chromium renderer process silently fails to apply the styles, indicating a deep-seated system conflict during graphical initialization.

This behavior persists even when launching with the most permissive flags: `npx electron . --no-sandbox --disable-site-isolation-trials --disable-features=RendererCodeIntegrity`.


Here is the diagnostic timeline section in a single markdown block, exactly as it appears in the final bug report:

```markdown
#### C. Final Electron Failure (The System Conflict)

Despite the code being proven correct and all components being embedded, the failure persists in the native Electron window.

| Step | Command Executed | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cache Clear & Relaunch** | `rm -rf ~/.config/flatpak-manifest-builder` then `npx electron . --no-sandbox` | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
| **Final Nuclear Launch** | `npx electron . --no-sandbox --disable-site-isolation-trials --disable-features=RendererCodeIntegrity` | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
| **CSS Fix** | All CSS was **embedded directly** into `index.html` to eliminate all external file access conflicts. | **Failure:** Still unstyled. |
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

## 🔗 Testcase Gist URL

**N/A (System-Level Conflict)**

A simple Electron Fiddle link cannot be provided because the application code has been confirmed to be **100% functional** and bug-free (tested working perfectly via `http-server` in Chrome and Firefox).

The failure is a **deep incompatibility** between the Chromium renderer (used by Electron v39) and the core Fedora/Gnome system libraries. **The bug cannot be reproduced in the clean, isolated context of Electron Fiddle**; it requires the specific library environment of the host system to fail.

We request attention based on the extensive diagnostic evidence provided in the "Diagnostic Timeline" section above.

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Introduce native support for multiple user profiles within the application, similar to Chrome/Chromium profile behavior. Each profile should maintain completely isolated sessions, storage, cookies, cache, and authentication state.

Without proper profile isolation, users must frequently log in and out, risking session conflicts and data leakage.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a profile system backed by Electron’s `session` partitions:
Each user profile maps to a unique persistent partition (e.g., `persist:userId`)

Full isolation of:
 - Cookies
 - LocalStorage / IndexedDB
 - Cache
 - Authentication tokens
 - Profiles persist across application restarts
 - Everything on application layer

Ability to:
 - Create new profiles
 - Switch between profiles without restarting the app
 - Delete profiles safely

### Alternatives Considered

trying to write an application with this feature, not sure how much is possible, but I think adding it to electron source itself will be great

### Additional Information

willing to work on this one

I am writing to formally report a series of critical issues affecting multiple Electron-based applications following the recent macOS update to version 26.1. These issues have severely impacted our business operations and productivity across the company.

Since updating to macOS Tahoe 26.1, we have consistently encountered the following problems across several widely used Electron-based applications, including Slack, Visual Studio Code, 1Password, and others:

- Frequent freezing and UI hangs, often requiring force-quitting the applications.
- Significant performance degradation, making basic tasks such as opening program windows, navigating menus, or loading workspaces slow or unresponsive.
- Malfunctions with file drag-and-drop functionality, including an inability to drag files into application windows and inconsistent behavior in different areas of the interface.
- Application launch failures, where applications either fail to start or crash immediately upon launch.
- General instability, which includes unexpected shutdowns, unresponsive interface components, and rendering issues.

I want to inform you that these issues are not new. We began experiencing similar issues after the previous macOS Tahoe update, and the release of version 26.1 has not resolved them. In many cases, the problems have become more widespread.

Critically, this is not an isolated incident. These issues now affect over one thousand users within our company, indicating that the problem is systemic and widespread across our environment.

Given our heavy reliance on Electron-based applications for essential daily workflows, the ongoing instability poses a significant challenge to maintaining efficient business operations.

I respectfully request that your  team:

1. Investigate the root cause of the issues introduced by the recent macOS Tahoe updates.
2. Provide an official statement outlining known issues, temporary workarounds, or recommended mitigation steps.
3. Offer information regarding potential patches or a projected timeline for resolving these problems.
